## Acceptance criteria (tag each one so claims can cite it)
- [AC-1] Never clean when it is not: every step that cannot do its job exits non-zero with a message naming the file or flag; no step exits 0 with a missing, empty, partial or stale output; no `--wait` reports done while a seat wrote nothing, read nothing or was cut off; no warning is silenced for a case it exists for.
- [AC-2] Blinding holds both ways: no seat or auditor can read, or is told, the peer's identity, files or labels, a vendor or model name, or the run folder's location, before the protocol allows it; the identity scan does not block on text derived from the target or the run's own folders.
- [AC-3] Numbers reconcile: every count a script prints equals an independent count from the files it came from.
- [AC-4] Recoverable, repeatable and clean: after any refused or interrupted step the run folder can be resumed or cleanly refused; nothing half-written; no child process survives a finished, failed, timed-out or stopped step; no seat keeps running after its answer; no console window per child on Windows; an unrelated process is never signalled (including a reused pid).
- [AC-5] Docs match scripts: every command, flag, default, exit code, file name and message in SKILL.md, references/, README, the task-packet template and each script's --help holds as written; nothing ties the skills to one project.
- [AC-6] Old runs still work: a run folder, manifest, notes file or packet written before these changes renders, rechecks and validates as before, except where a change says otherwise.
- [AC-7] Weight: code, flags, files or doc paragraphs that can be removed with no loss. At most 3 claims per seat.
- [AC-8] Field feedback fixed: every finding in the feedback files (`C:/Users/dev/cross-review-runs/closing-r5/evidence/feedback/`: linux-1-BUGS.md, linux-2-report.md, linux-3-selfreview.md, mac-1-findings-for-dev.md, mac-2-round5-report.md, macos-3-selfreview.md) is fixed on the code as it is now, or is listed under Known deviations with a reason that still holds. A fix that closes the reported input but leaves a sibling input of the same shape open is PARTLY CONFIRMED.
- [AC-9] No regression from a fix: every narrowed pattern, deleted check or removed line in the diff keeps accepting what it accepted before, unless the change says otherwise. For each such change you checked, name one real input the old line handled and the new line mishandles (a finding), or say no such input exists and why.
- [AC-10] Tests prove the fixes: a test that still passes with its fix reverted, or that checks only the input the fix was written for while a sibling input of the same shape is untested, is a finding (LOW, or MEDIUM when the untested input is broken).

## Known deviations from the criteria
Accepted, not to be reported again unless the description below is no longer accurate:
- Decided: a line that starts with a "blocked:" label counts as the seat's own block in any form outside a code fence; a seat that quotes someone else's `Blocked:` line that way is stopped and asked again. Mid-sentence "blocked:" is not read. A seat that lies in its `Blocked:` line is not detected. A seat with claims that declares a block ends COMPLETE with a "may have reviewed blind" caveat (Linux report item 8): pending the maintainer's decision, so do not report it again.
- Decided: a bare (unquoted) path with a space is read up to the space (the template asks for backticks); an endpoint written as `name.ending:port` with no scheme is not probed. A missed or false ADVISORY warning from the packet path scan, the reach probe or the missing-`Blocked:`-line warning is LOW; so is the phase1 reach warning that ignores an earlier probe's OK lines (Linux report item 11).
- `review-run` passes `--timeout 0` (no limit) for a CLI seat that never answers; a seat that answered and then hangs is stopped 30 s after its answer. OpenCode seats keep close-only completion (no verified final event).
- A background job a seat's tool command started that outlives the seat CLI and holds its output is not stopped by the dispatcher: on Linux/macOS when it left the process group (Linux report item 3), on Windows when its parent chain is broken (the previous round's F4: the parent-chain scan cannot reach it; only a Windows job object would, which is pending the maintainer's decision). The run warns (`stopIncomplete`, a report caveat). A bind-mount spelling of the run folder is not detected by the guard (Linux report item 5). The seat brief forbids leaving a background process.
- Decided: a run-folder path broken across two lines, or shortened in prose (`C:\...\run`, `<runs>/r5`), is caught by neither the rewrite nor the guard; a `| Blocked: none |` table row is neither none nor a block (a No findings seat is asked again); a seat that cites its own scratch folder through `~` or a variable is refused and asked again (safe direction).
- LOW only: a No findings seat that contradicts itself (a strict `Blocked: none` line, then a block written in a form the reader does not take); a false stop or a missed match where a folder name ends next to an unusual character (the shared `NAME_CONTINUES` boundary): the run stops and asks again, or a peer sees the placeholder-free path of a sibling folder.
- On Windows each preflight `--exec` command costs about 5 to 7 seconds more on a busy machine (PowerShell start-up of the job wrapper); `--timeout` counts that time. A wrapper killed during its start-up can rarely stay in a kernel wait that only a reboot clears (seen once on this host, from a test with a short timeout); this is the host, not a defect, unless you show the skill causing it.
- A review in progress across an update that used an isolated copy must be restarted (CHANGELOG upgrade note). The plugin version stays 1.1.0 for this content: the bump is the maintainer's release decision.
- A seat or auditor that runs as a native agent also sees the host's own instructions and memory; `review-config seats` prints a note; CLI seats are the documented way around it.
- Two LOW leftovers: a path inside `__...__` emphasis with a `<br>` inside it is missed; the 10-line output cap can hide the "no Blocked: line" warning when stop notes fill it.
- The shallow-seat warning compares claims and web use, not run duration. `exchange.mjs prepare`: when it stops half-way, its message gives the manual recovery steps. A read-only seat cannot run the test suite itself: the documented route is the preflight evidence logs. Output tokens of native Claude agents are unknown; the round count follows one chain of re-reviews; a REVIEW.md only the branch added is named and not used; Codex text in result.json is UTF-8.
- Known flaky under load, not a finding by itself: the detach tests "five consecutive workers" and "--detach returns at once", claude-dispatch "an isolated seat writing the real target by absolute path", the codex mcp-hang test and the opencode `--isolate` test; a failure that also happens when the file runs alone is a finding.
- By design: a finding marked "wrong" leaves every count and list; a file-name or ambiguous partial-path Where match never regroups a finding; the scratch folder is named in the brief but created by the seat.

## Checks
- Run tests and repros only in a disposable copy outside the target, or by importing the shipped module from the target without writing into it, with TMPDIR/TEMP pointed at your own scratch folder.
- Evidence rules: execute before you claim (a HIGH needs the input, command and output); prove reachability from a supported route; sweep the class and list every site; for every narrowed or removed line (AC-9) say what it used to accept; for a process claim show the process list before and after.
- For each hypothesis, try at least one sibling input of the same shape besides the one named; for an input-shape claim, a matrix of at least 10 shapes.
- Coverage line in `## Checks performed`: read fully / read partly / not read.
- Proposals: the smallest change that closes the defect, lines named; no new flag, mode, file or dependency unless the defect needs it; no style claims.
Run single test files (`node --test scripts/tests/<name>.test.mjs`) in the foreground, not the whole suite at once.

## Severity note
HIGH: a blocked or blind reviewer reported as clean, a blinding leak, a lost or overwritten run, worktree or target file, a process left running after a step or a run, a console window per child, a kill of an unrelated process, a wrong number in a report a reader acts on. MEDIUM: a step that exits 0 when it should stop, a wrong result or count, a doc that misleads, a portability problem that blocks a normal user on a common setup. LOW: a missed or false ADVISORY warning (the packet-path "does not exist" note, a reach-probe item, the missing-`Blocked:`-line warning), an AC-7 weight claim, anything minor. A field-feedback fix that does not hold for the reported input is at least the feedback's own severity. Every HIGH and CRITICAL claim states its Trigger (what input or state makes it happen, and how often a real run meets it). The reader is the maintainer deciding what to fix before the next release.
